title: LLM Cold Start Optimization
summary: Shorten the path from a scheduled inference replica to usable capacity by measuring and optimizing each initialization stage.
overview: LLM cold start is the delay before a new serving instance can accept useful work. It includes scheduling, image retrieval, model download, deserialization, accelerator allocation, kernel compilation or graph capture, tokenizer setup, and warmup. Optimizing only container startup can leave model readiness unchanged.

The right strategy depends on demand and infrastructure: cached artifacts, smaller images, prebuilt compatible engines, local model storage, and a minimum warm pool address different stages. Readiness must reflect actual inference capability, while startup probes allow legitimate initialization without restart loops. A warm process with an unloaded model is not warm capacity.

production.poc: A prototype records timestamps for every initialization stage and runs one representative warmup request.
production.production: Production pins artifacts, caches model files safely, separates startup from readiness, and keeps enough warm capacity for the latency objective.
production.scale: Enterprise scale coordinates model placement, rollout surge capacity, cache invalidation, and regional warm pools without exhausting accelerator quota.

components.name: Artifact cache
components.role: Provides verified images and model weights near the serving node.

components.name: Placement scheduler
components.role: Selects compatible accelerators and available memory.

components.name: Runtime initializer
components.role: Loads weights and prepares kernels and execution state.

components.name: Warmup runner
components.role: Exercises representative shapes and verifies a usable output.

components.name: Readiness controller
components.role: Admits traffic only after initialization and capacity checks pass.

flow.title: Measure startup stages
flow.description: Separate scheduling delay, artifact transfer, model loading, and runtime preparation.

flow.title: Place compatible capacity
flow.description: Schedule onto nodes with the required hardware and sufficient headroom.

flow.title: Load verified artifacts
flow.description: Use checksummed local caches or efficient transfer without mixing model revisions.

flow.title: Prepare the runtime
flow.description: Allocate model and cache memory and compile supported execution paths as needed.

flow.title: Warm representative requests
flow.description: Exercise realistic prompt shapes and verify output and resource stability.

flow.title: Publish readiness
flow.description: Add the replica to routing only when it can meet its initial admission contract.

useCase.title: Preparing capacity for scheduled campaigns
useCase.situation: A retailer expects bursts of assistant traffic when new promotions go live.
useCase.problem: Reactive scaling starts model replicas too late, causing queues during the first minutes of demand.
useCase.requirement: Have usable inference capacity ready before the predictable burst without keeping the entire peak fleet warm all day.
useCase.architecture: A scheduled capacity plan preloads approved artifacts and warms a bounded replica pool.
runtime: Before campaign launch, nodes cache the model and run representative requests.
The router admits traffic only after readiness and token-capacity checks pass.
useCase.failure: If a new artifact fails warmup, existing warm replicas continue serving while the rollout pauses.
useCase.impact: Measure time to usable capacity, first-request latency, and idle warm-pool cost; container-running status is not the service objective.

tradeoffs.cost: Requires storage, integrity, and eviction policies.
May depend on specific hardware and runtime versions.

failures.detection: Loading succeeds partially but warmup fails.
failures.recovery: Verify complete artifact-runtime compatibility and purge only the invalid revision.
Set startup thresholds from measured worst-case initialization.

mistakes.fix: Instrument the full path to successful inference.
Keep readiness false until representative execution passes.
Include queue growth and startup lead time.

whenToUse: Use when model loading dominates availability of new capacity.
whenNotToUse: Avoid expensive warm pools for delay-tolerant sparse jobs.
Do not reuse compiled artifacts across unsupported hardware.
Avoid masking failed warmup with permissive readiness.
checklist: Configure separate startup and readiness checks.
Measure idle cost against latency benefit.
